findings.title: GET /delete/<id> reports success for a post that does not exist
findings.property: deleting a nonexistent (or already deleted) post does not report 'Post Deleted' with status 1; it is a 404 or status 0
findings.input: logged in, no posts, GET /delete/1 (or a second GET /delete/1 after deleting post 1)
findings.expected: 404 or JSON status 0 (error), since nothing was deleted
findings.actual: 200 {"message": "Post Deleted", "status": 1} and flash 'The entry was deleted.'
findings.evidence: The handler's own result dict defaults to {status: 0, message: 'Error'} and sets status 1 'Post Deleted' unconditionally after query.delete(), ignoring the returned row count. REST convention: deleting an unknown id gives 404, and a repeat delete is 404.

review.title: GET /delete/<id> returns status 1 when no row matches
review.reason: The existing test `test_delete_message` in tests/app_test.py logs in and calls `/delete/1` and expects `status == 1`. The `client` fixture is not shown adding any post first, so the test appears to cover this exact case of deleting a post that was never created. This suggests the project treats delete as idempotent and the 'Post Deleted' result is intended. The 404-on-missing-id behaviour is the reporter's REST assumption, since the project does not document it, and a maintainer would likely reject a change that breaks the existing test.
